audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagree between layers. Full: Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Zed/Skill/Zed. Content: Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Zed/Akshan.
audit.why: 52.35% over 2575 games supports Akshan early — the three-hit string plus its shield beats Zed at contact — but level 6 is unambiguously Zed's, first item is even, and late Zed picks the isolated target.
audit.corrected: Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Zed / Skill / Zed, proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item and late spikes were both built on W camouflage dodging Death Mark's burst.
audit.why: Death Mark repeats a portion of the damage Zed dealt to the target while marked. Going camouflaged does not remove the mark or reduce what already landed. The counterplay is taking less damage inside the three seconds — which is Heroic Swing, 800 range, out of his 290-range Shadow Slash.
audit.corrected: Akshan's real spikes are the level 3 swing and, at parity, first item; Zed's are 6 and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Zed 'has no ranged poke' and that 'you out-range his Q'. It also invents a 'marked auto' from Akshan's kit.
audit.why: Razor Shuriken is 900 range on a flat 6-second cooldown — it outranges Avengerang's 850. Akshan applies no mark of any kind; his passive is a three-hit proc with a shield. Telling a player to win a poke war they lose is the most damaging kind of wrong advice here.
audit.corrected: You lose the ranged exchange and win at contact; Living Shadow is 20 seconds at rank 1 and is also his only escape, so a shadow thrown forward is a Zed with no way out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zed.json Q range 900 cd 6, W cd 20/19/18/17/16

audit.whatIsWrong: Death Mark was tracked everywhere without its cooldown, and Shadow Slash's range was never given.
audit.why: Death Mark is 120/110/100 — a countable window. Shadow Slash is 290 range on a 5-to-3 second cooldown, which is why ending a swing next to him is fatal.
audit.corrected: Numbers now stated in the mid, late and dos/donts text.

edits.before: Akshan's first item and W camouflage let him dodge or punish that Death Mark burst, restoring his advantage.
edits.after: First item is even: Death Mark is 120 seconds, and outside it his Razor Shuriken still outranges you.

edits.after: Late, Death Mark falls to 100 seconds and he chooses the isolated target, which is usually you.

edits.before: Zed can't shadow-dash into your Avengerang range without eating a marked auto and Q proc, so your poke wins the early trade window every time.
edits.after: Razor Shuriken outranges your boomerang at 900 to 850, so win at contact instead: Living Shadow is 20 seconds and it is his escape too.

edits.before: Zed's Death Mark all-in is the one moment he can burst through your kit before your R comes back up, especially if he catches you pushed out of position.
edits.after: Death Mark makes Zed untargetable as he dashes in and repeats a portion of the damage he deals over the next 3 seconds — the counter is taking less, not vanishing.

edits.before: Your passive burst and W camouflage let you dodge his follow-up shadow swap and punish him hard once your first item lands.
edits.after: Once your first item lands, the swing is what beats his shadow swap — 800 range of exit while he is still 650 from his own shadow.

edits.before: Comeuppance shreds Zed's isolated flank attempts in teamfights, and your E gives you an escape his shadow dash can't easily chase down.
edits.after: Late, Death Mark is 100 seconds and he hunts isolated targets — Heroic Swing is your answer, since Living Shadow only reaches 650.

edits.before: Zed has no way to close on you without walking his shadow through your Avengerang zone, and every dash attempt eats a marked auto plus passive proc. You out-range his Q in minion-clear trades and can punish his shadow cooldown windows with Heroic Swing repositioning. Play patient — short trades favor you heavily as long as you don't overextend past minion wave.
edits.after: Razor Shuriken is 900 range to your 850, so you do not win the poke war — you win at contact, where the three-hit string and its shield beat anything he has before 6. Living Shadow is 20 seconds at rank 1 and doubles as his escape, so the moment he throws it forward he has no way out. Stay level with the wave and never step past it.

edits.before: Lvl 6 is Zed's window: Death Mark's delayed burst can catch you out if your R is down or you're caught away from minions, letting him punish a bad recall or push. Track his ultimate cooldown and don't get isolated near brush he can shadow into. From Lvl 7 onward your passive stacking and poke put you back in control, since Zed still lacks any ranged follow-up outside his ult.
edits.after: Level 6 is Zed's: Death Mark makes him untargetable on the way in and detonates 3 seconds later for a share of everything he landed, so the fight is about what he lands in those 3 seconds. It is 120 seconds at rank 1 — count it and do not be alone when it is up. From 7 on, trade at contact and use the swing early, because it is 18 seconds and he only needs one window.

edits.before: Once your first item is online you dodge his Death Mark burst window with W's camouflage and punish the whiff hard with your own passive damage. In teamfights, Comeuppance picks off any Zed who commits to a flank, and Heroic Swing lets you disengage faster than his shadow can chase. Play around his ultimate timer and you consistently come out ahead.
edits.after: Camouflage does not remove Death Mark — the mark repeats a share of what he deals while it is on you, so the answer is Heroic Swing out of his 290-range Shadow Slash, not vanishing in place. Living Shadow only reaches 650, so a swing off terrain leaves him standing in the open. Play his 100-second ultimate timer and you come out ahead.

edits.before: That’s Zed’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.

notes: Worst error here was the range claim: the page told the player Zed has no ranged poke and that Akshan out-ranges his Q. Razor Shuriken is 900 to Avengerang's 850 on a flat 6-second cooldown, so the poke war is Zed's — Akshan wins at contact. Also removed the invented 'marked auto' (Akshan marks nothing) and the repeated claim that W camouflage dodges Death Mark's burst — the mark repeats damage already dealt and stealth does not touch it. Chart disagreed on six of seven rows and is proposed as one atomic group. breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.wave, breakdown.late, breakdown.feeding, ahead, tradeGood and tradeBad remain shared Akshan boilerplate; I had nothing further Zed-specific to ground them in beyond the points already placed.
